reasons: Deletes and merges real rows and depends on hard-coded ID lists.
The file is a one-time script and has been run once or planned to run.

terms.meaning: a saved copy of rows before they are changed, so they can be restored
moving one row's linked data to another row and then deleting the first row
the project's rule for writing a date that is only roughly known

used_by: Run by hand from the api-server folder

sections.name: File setup, JUNK
sections.title: Setup and the rows to delete
sections.what: Loads libraries and lists the 29 project IDs that came from news headlines and are to be deleted.
sections.why: The header says these rows were parsed from headlines and are not real projects.
sections.watch_out: The ID list is fixed text; a wrong ID would delete the wrong project.

sections.name: MERGE
sections.title: Duplicate-to-survivor map
sections.what: Pairs each duplicate nuclear row with the reactor row that should keep its data.
sections.why: The header says these are legacy seed rows for the same reactors.
sections.watch_out: A wrong pair would move evidence to the wrong reactor.

sections.name: PLANT_ROWS
sections.title: Plant-level rows and the templated-text rules
sections.what: Names the two plant-level rows and defines patterns for templated labels and example.com placeholder URLs.
sections.why: Plant-level rows may describe a whole plant, so their merged evidence gets a note.
sections.watch_out: A label pattern that is too broad could deactivate real evidence.

sections.name: DEPENDENT, iso
sections.title: Tables linked to projects
sections.what: Lists every table that stores rows keyed to a project, so they can be moved or deleted together.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the header, which says they move with the project.
sections.watch_out: A new project-linked table not in this list would be left pointing at a deleted project.

sections.name: statesUsdMillions, pool, report
sections.title: Quote check for USD amounts and the logging helper
sections.what: Checks whether a quote states a given dollar amount, and defines the helper that writes change log rows.
sections.why: Used to decide whether a stored value is backed by its quote.
sections.watch_out: The pattern only handles a few dollar spellings.

sections.name: log (part 1)
sections.title: Backup, junk delete and merge (part 1)
sections.what: Opens the transaction, checks that the expected junk rows exist and look right, backs them up, deletes them with their linked rows, and starts merging duplicates.
sections.why: The backup is written before any delete, so the delete can be undone.
sections.watch_out: Stops with an error if the number or names of rows do not match.

sections.name: log: for
sections.title: Deactivate placeholder evidence
sections.what: Loops over nuclear evidence and turns off quotes that are templated labels or cite example.com.
sections.why: The header says these quotes are not text from a real page.
sections.watch_out: Deactivated quotes stay in the database and can be turned back on.

sections.name: log: if
sections.title: Clear values no quote supports and move dates
sections.what: Clears nuclear budget and delay values that no quote states, and moves oil-gas and lithium actual completion dates to the updated completion column.
sections.why: Seed values with no source are removed, and the header says actual completion was stored in the planned date column.
sections.watch_out: Date moves that cannot be resolved leave cod_date empty on purpose.

summary: One-off repair of the nuclear rows in the Yard: deletes news-headline rows, merges duplicates into the correct reactor rows, removes placeholder evidence, clears unsupported values, and moves oil-gas and lithium dates to the right columns.
purpose: Fixes data errors found by a sanity audit so nuclear and oil-gas figures match what the sources say.
why: The header says the change was requested by the owner after the audit.
how: Opens a transaction, backs up every row it will touch into a compressed file, deletes or merges rows, deactivates unsupported evidence, clears values no quote states, and moves dates. Without --commit it rolls back. It writes a JSON report.
inputs: The projects, evidence and dependent tables, the DATABASE_URL setting, and the --commit flag.
outputs: A compressed backup, a JSON report under data/repairs, and change log rows when committed.
risks: Deletes project rows. A wrong entry in the JUNK or MERGE lists would remove real data. The backup is the only way back.
debug: Read the backup file and the report's junkDeleted, merged and valuesCleared lists. Run without --commit first.
